full_judgment:
2. The facts of the case, in brief, are that the writ petitioner-respondent herein obtained her degree of M.B.B.S. from Mymensingh Medical College in 1981. In 1984, she joined Bangladesh Red Crescent Society as Medical Officer and was entrusted with the responsibility of coordinator of RHIYA project. She successfully performed her functions as Medical Officer (Health Division) and Coordination and got appreciation from various international organizations, like EU Parliament members. EU midterm evaluation team, etc., which was communicated to the concerned authority, but it created enmity in the mind of her superior authority. 

 6. Respondent Nos.1-3 entered appearance by filing affidavit-in-opposition. Their case is that there were numerous allegations brought against the writ petitioner and subsequently she was found guilty by a properly constituted Enquiry Committee. The writ petitioner was appointed in the RHIYA project as a Project Coordinator and the position was temporary in nature. As a result, the position was abolished when the project ended. The writ petitioner was simply a Medical Officer, whereas the project Director was a Director of the Health Division. In the hierarchy of Red Crescent Society, a Medical Officer cannot directly or indirectly occupy the position of a Director. Hence, the allegation as alleged by the writ petitioner is baseless. 

 8. Mr. S.M. Rezaul Karim, learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner submitted that the High Court Division erred in law in passing the impugned judgement and order, inasmuch as the said order would hamper, hinder and encumber the general activities of Bangladesh Red Crescent Society, which is detrimental to the interest of business communities, as such the impugned judgement and order passed by the High Court Division is liable to be set aside. He further submitted that the fact as alleged by the respondent-writ petitioner is a disputed one and it is a settled principle that writ jurisdiction is not a proper forum for settling a disputed question of fact; conversely, it is not amenable to writ jurisdiction, because the writ petitioner failed to adduce sufficient documents/evidence in support of her contention. In 42 DLR (AD) 126, at page 130 it has been emphasised that "if the assertion made by the Petitioner is not supported by materials to the satisfaction of the Court, the Court may refuse to act on such assertion alone", as such the impugned judgement and order passed by the High Court Division is liable to be set aside. The learned Advocate also submitted that the writ petitioner furnished false and fabricated vouchers to writ respondent No.3 on 04.4.2006 to adjust the advanced money taken by her, and that writ respondent No. 3 looking at the bills and not seeing the signatures of the field workers, had a doubt and enquired into the matter and found the bills to be false and fabricated, and as such raised objection. A four member enquiry committee was constituted by decision of the authority of the Bangladesh Red Crescent Society. The respondent-writ petitioner made an objection against Dr. Md. Aytal Haque, Member, Enquiry Committee, as such, he was replaced by Mr. S.M. Rafiqul Islam, Director, Unit Affairs by the order vide Memo No. HS-4201/06 dated 9th May 2006. The said Enquiry Committee took evidence of 7 (seven) witnesses (employees of RHIYA project) and also of the writ petitioner, writ respondent No. 3 and of the then Acting Secretary General, over four days. The said Enquiry Committee sub-mitted a report on 28.5.2006, where it has been manifested that the respondent/writ petitioner is responsible, and accountable for submission of false vouchers, misreporting, dishonesty with the Society's business, and in such state of affairs, the respondent-writ petitioner already deposited Tk.89,500/- in the account of RHIYA, BDRCS on 17.7.2006 in Sonali Bank. Hence, the High Court Division erred in law in passing the impugned judgement and order. He sub-mitted that after receiving the enquiry report and when the Chairman of the Society accepted it, the writ respondent No.2 issued the show cause notice on 17.9.2006 and passed the impugned order on 13.11.2006, as such, the impugned order as passed was within time, inasmuch as, for the misappropriation of the Project's Fund and mismanagement of the Project by the respondent-writ petitioner, the RHIYA Project has not been extended. Hence, the respondent-writ petitioner cannot be posted in her previous post of Coordinator of RHIYA Project. As such, the High Court Division has misread, misconstrued and misunderstood the materials on record and consequently failed to comprehend the facts of the case and misapplied the law, thus the impugned judgment and order passed by the High Court Division calls for interference by this Division. He submitted that earlier another Enquiry Committee was formed vide Office Order No. S.G-1011/04 dated 27.7.2004 for a separate allegation made against the respondent-writ petitioner and as such report was submitted on 8.9.2004, while the said committee found her blameworthy, accountable and at fault along with commentaries to the effect that: 

 9. The facts of the aforesaid enquiry and its report was suppressed by the respondent-writ petitioner in the writ petition. Hence, the High Court Division failed to appreciate the facts and circumstances of this case in its true perspective, as a result of which there has been serious miscarriage of justice and as such the impugned judgment and order passed by the High Court Division is liable to be set aside. The learned Advocate submitted that the enquiry committee was constituted with the governance, i.e. the highest authority of the Society and on their recommendation the respondent-writ petitioner was dismissed from service, as such when she filed an appeal, the Chairman of the Society took decision in the following terms: 

 And as such the said order was already communicated vide letter dated 31.1.2007 to the respondent-writ petitioner, while the High Court Division acted unlawfully giving relief under its Special Original Jurisdiction, as such the impugned judgment and order passed by the High Court Division calls for interference by this Division. He lastly submitted that the High Court Division misdirected itself in the facts and circumstances of the case and most non judiciously and arbitrarily passed the impugned judgement and order, thus the same is liable to be set aside. 

 13. The High Court Division also observed that the writ petitioner did not receive any copy of the report of the board of inquiry, although there is provision to communicate the same to the petitioner within ten working days from the date of receipt of the report. The High Court Division further observed that in case of failure of the authority to take a final decision in a case under this rule within 90 working days, from the date of the allegation against the accused, the allegation against the accused shall stand withdrawn and the proceedings shall be disposed of. In the instant case the allegation was brought against the writ petitioner on 17.04.2006 and 142 working days had elapsed. In such circumstances, the High Court Division took the view that the impugned order of removal from service was illegal and violative of the provision of law.
